q: For AS operations, what is the maximum number of Flight Crewmembers on a pairing who may have less than 150 hours line operating flight time in type and crew position?
a: Only one Flight Crewmember (CA, F/O, IRO) may have less than 150 hours line operating flight time (including OE) at the Company in type and crew position (seat).

src.quote: only one Flight Crewmember (CA, F/O, IRO) may have less than: (AS) 150 hours line operating flight time at the Company (including Operating Experience, "OE") in type and crew position (seat).
src.note: Applies to all operations under 14 CFR 121.438. The HA equivalent threshold is 100 hours line operating flight time in type.

q: How many hours in type must a qualified Check Pilot have to be exempt from the crew pairing requirement while performing Check Pilot duties?

src.quote: A qualified Check Pilot with at least 75 hours in type is not subject to this pairing requirement while performing Check Pilot duties.
src.note: The exemption applies only while the Check Pilot is actually performing Check Pilot duties.

q: First Officers with less than how many hours in aircraft type at Alaska Airlines may not make takeoffs or landings at special airports?
a: First Officers with less than 100 hours in aircraft type at Alaska Airlines shall not make takeoffs or landings at special airports.

src.quote: First Officers with less than 100 hours in aircraft type at Alaska Airlines shall not make takeoffs or landings at special airports
src.note: FAA Special Airports are marked "Airport Qualification" on the Jeppesen 19-XX chart; "Airport Familiarization" charts carry no qualification/currency requirement.

q: To satisfy PIC Special Airport currency by making a takeoff or landing to that airport, what ceiling and visibility conditions must exist?
a: The ceiling must be at least 1000 ft above the lowest MEA or MOCA, or initial approach altitude prescribed for the instrument approach for that airport, and visibility at least 3 miles.

src.quote: Make a takeoff or landing to that airport if the ceiling at that airport is at least 1000 ft above the lowest MEA or MOCA, or initial approach altitude prescribed for the instrument approach for that airport and the visibility is at least 3 miles.
src.note: Alternatively, currency may be re-established within the preceding 12 calendar months by an aircraft/level-D sim entry or by reviewing the FAA-accepted Jeppesen FD Pro airport pictorials.

q: How often must a pilot accomplish a NAT HLA segment as a required Flight Crewmember to maintain North Atlantic High-Level Airspace currency on the 787?
a: At least one NAT HLA segment every 24 months.

src.ref: FOM 3.3.4 — North Atlantic High-Level Airspace (NAT HLA) Qualification (787)
src.quote: Pilots are required to accomplish at least one NAT HLA segment as a required Flight Crewmember every 24 months.
src.note: NAT HLA qualification applies to qualified PICs and SICs; see the applicable FOTM for the requirements to re-establish currency once it lapses.

q: For Consolidation, how many hours of line operating flight time must Captains and First Officers acquire, and within what period of their Qual LOE in type?
a: 100 hours of line operating flight time at Alaska Airlines within 120 days of their Qual LOE in type (flight time includes OE).

src.quote: Captains and First Officers must acquire 100 hours of line operating flight time at Alaska Airlines within 120 days of their Qual LOE in type.
src.note: Prior consolidation in type as PIC or SIC satisfies the requirement for all seats in that aircraft type. Resting time on augmented flights cannot be counted toward consolidation.

q: For consolidation on augmented flights, how much of the flight segment's total hours is subtracted for double augment versus single augment?
a: 50% is subtracted for double augment and 33% for single augment.

src.quote: For augmented crews, the total hours of the flight segment will be subtracted as follows: 50% for double augment 33% for single augment
src.note: Time spent resting, while not seated at the controls, cannot count toward OE or consolidation requirements.

q: To qualify for Captain Upgrade, how many hours SIC at the Company must a pilot have?
a: 1000 hours SIC at the Company, or the pilot must meet the requirements listed in 14 CFR 121.436.

src.quote: To qualify for Captain Upgrade, a pilot must have 1000 hours SIC at the Company or meet the requirements listed in 14 CFR 121.436.
src.note: The upgrade requirement is governed by 14 CFR 121.436.

q: Under the Initial First Officer takeoff/landing restrictions, at what crosswind component must the Captain make all takeoffs and landings (unless the FO is paired with a Check Pilot)?
a: When the crosswind component is greater than 15 kts (for a First Officer with less than 100 hours in aircraft type).

src.ref: FOM 3.6 — Initial First Officer Restrictions – Takeoff and Landing
src.quote: The crosswind component is greater than 15 kts
src.note: The Captain must also make all takeoffs and landings at special airports, on contaminated runways, when braking action is less than GOOD, when windshear is reported nearby, or when visibility is at or below 3/4 sm or RVR at or below 4000.

q: A High Minimums Captain is any Captain with less than how many hours as PIC in type at the Company?
a: Less than 100 hours as a PIC in type at the Company.

src.quote: High minimums apply to any Captain who has less than 100 hours as a PIC in type at the Company.
src.note: The Captain must advise Dispatch of high minimums status prior to each flight segment when weather is reported or forecast below 1000 ft ceiling and 3 miles visibility at or near time of landing.

q: For military charter operations, what combined minimum total flight hours in the aircraft type must the Captain and First Officer have?
a: A combined minimum of 250 total flight hours in the aircraft type (except for aircraft new to the Company).

src.ref: FOM 3.8 — High Minimums Crewmembers – Military Charters
src.quote: The Captain and First Officer must have a combined minimum of 250 total flight hours in the aircraft type except for aircraft new to the Company, to operate any military charter operations.
src.note: This requirement stems from 32 CFR 861 governing military charter operations.

q: How many hours as PIC in type at the Company must a Captain have to perform CAT III operations, and is it reducible?
a: A minimum of 100 hours as PIC in type at the Company, and it is not reducible.

src.ref: FOM 3.15 — Category III Operations – Captain Hours Required
src.quote: Captain must have minimum of 100 hours as PIC in type at the Company (not reducible) to perform CAT III operations.
src.note: During Captain OE, CAT III is not authorized for the qualifying Captain unless they had previously met this hours requirement.

q: For SA CAT I / CAT II operations under Exemption 5549, how many hours as a pilot in a turbojet aircraft must the Captain have?
a: A minimum of 300 hours as a pilot (PIC or SIC) in a turbojet aircraft.

src.ref: FOM 3.16.2 — SA CAT I/CAT II Operations at Destination or Alternate
src.quote: The Captain has a minimum of 300 hours as a pilot (PIC or SIC) in a turbojet aircraft
src.note: For AS the Captain must also comply with the SA CAT I/II Approach Briefing Card; HGS Experience Card completion is not required.

q: During Captain/First Officer OE takeoffs, at what RVR must the left seat occupant conduct all takeoffs?
a: The left seat occupant will conduct all takeoffs when the RVR is 1600 ft or less.

src.quote: The left seat occupant will conduct all takeoffs when the RVR is 1600 ft or less.
src.note: During OE the Check Pilot is the Company-designated PIC and must occupy a pilot seat.

q: What is the Takeoff and Landing Currency requirement, including the currency interval and any limit on Autolands?
a: At least 3 takeoffs and landings within 90 days, in the specific aircraft type or an AS-approved simulator, in either seat; only one of the required landings may be an Autoland. Documented by ACARS entry.

src.ref: FOM 3.19 — Operational Currency and Training Requirements
src.quote: At least 3 takeoffs and landings in: Specific aircraft type or an AS-approved simulator supervised by an AS Instructor or Check Pilot Either seat Only one of the required landings may be an Autoland.
src.note: The currency interval is 90 days; credit for an Autoland landing may go to both the Captain and First Officer.

q: Under Exemption 5549, if the crosswind component exceeds 15 kts combined with a braking action report of less than 'good,' what minimum visibility is required?
a: Visibility must be at least 4000 RVR (3/4 mile visibility).

src.ref: FOM 3.16.1 — CAT I Precision Approach at Destination or Alternate
src.quote: If the crosswind component exceeds 15 kts combined with a braking action report of less than "good," visibility must be at least 4000 RVR (3/4 mile visibility).
src.note: For AS the approach is flown by the Captain with autopilot coupled (dual channel on a CAT II/III runway only) or following HGS AIII guidance to DA/DH.

q: CHECK-AIRMAN SCENARIO: You're a 787 First Officer and monthly bid closure is tomorrow. A check airman notices your last takeoff and landing was 91 days ago, so your Takeoff and Landing Currency has lapsed. Under FOM 3.19, what happens to next month's bid and how do you correct the deficiency?
a: Because the currency requirement was not maintained, the following month's bid will not be honored and you will be removed from flight duty and payroll until the deficiency is corrected. Currency deficiencies are corrected by submission of appropriate Training Certification Forms, simulator requalification, or supervised line flying.

src.ref: FOM 3.19 — Operational Currency and Training Requirements
src.quote: Failure to initially accomplish and/or maintain currency requirements will result in the following month's bid not being honored and will result in removal from flight duty and payroll until any deficiencies are corrected.
src.note: Operational currency and training requirements must be accomplished prior to monthly bid closure; Takeoff and Landing Currency is documented by ACARS entry.

q: CHECK-AIRMAN SCENARIO: A check airman reviews your last 90 days and finds 3 takeoffs and landings in the 787 — but 2 of the 3 landings were Autolands. Are you legally current for Takeoff and Landing Currency under FOM 3.19, and why or why not?
a: No. Only one of the three required landings may be an Autoland, so at least two must be hand-flown landings. With two Autolands you are one manual landing short and are not current.

src.ref: FOM 3.19 — Operational Currency and Training Requirements
src.quote: At least 3 takeoffs and landings in: Specific aircraft type or an AS-approved simulator supervised by an AS Instructor or Check Pilot Either seat Only one of the required landings may be an Autoland.
src.note: Landings may be in the specific aircraft type or an AS-approved simulator, in either seat; credit for an Autoland landing may go to both the Captain and First Officer.

q: CHECK-AIRMAN SCENARIO: Scheduling wants to assign you as a required Flight Crewmember on a 787 segment through North Atlantic High-Level Airspace, but your last NAT HLA segment was 25 months ago. Under FOM 3.3.4, are you current for NAT HLA, and what governs re-establishing it?
a: No. NAT HLA currency requires accomplishing at least one NAT HLA segment as a required Flight Crewmember every 24 months; at 25 months your currency has lapsed. Re-establishing currency is governed by the applicable FOTM.

src.ref: FOM 3.3.4 — North Atlantic High-Level Airspace (NAT HLA) Qualification (787)
src.quote: Pilots are required to accomplish at least one NAT HLA segment as a required Flight Crewmember every 24 months.
src.note: NAT HLA qualification applies to qualified PICs and SICs on the 787; see the applicable FOTM for the requirements to re-establish currency once it lapses.
